title: How Jacky Chou grows Local Rank: community-led funnel, YouTube-first launch and local SEO levers
summary: Jacky Chou explains how Local Rank sells software by first building a paid education community, gating free checklists on X, and using YouTube to launch. He also covers local SEO ranking levers (reviews, citations, CTR) and how to sell local SEO to high-CPC niches.

principles.text: When the market is tiny, educate people to create new buyers (build the TAM) instead of only selling to existing ones.
principles.quote: the local SEO space is so small. It's it's super small. So what we have to do is we have to start educating people. We have to like build the actual TAM.

principles.text: Software with a learning curve sells better through a community that teaches with the tool than by pushing the product directly.
principles.quote: I realized you can't just raw dog push people into local rank. It's like too hard for people to use. So, we have to have a lot of education.

principles.text: Run the paid community at break-even to fund ads; the software upsell is the profit.
principles.quote: we try to run the community at break even and then the software is like the gravy.

principles.text: Talk about a topic on YouTube for a long time before launching; the built audience makes the launch pop.
principles.quote: if you talk about something for a year and then you launch a product about that topic, it's going to it's it's going to pop no matter what.

principles.text: Give away gated free checklists on X: comment-to-get engagement bait, then email capture, VSL, retargeting and a long email flow.
principles.quote: We don't even give we don't even give the template right away. They have to give us their email for us to give them the template. And guess what happens after the sign up? VSSL right away and then hella retargeting

principles.text: Being your own customer (doing the service you sell) creates a product moat that feature-copiers can't match.
principles.quote: we actually do the thing right so like we actually do local SEO what I found is I I I think that's actually our moat
